llm.summary: The skill is a small, local CLI-style collection of helper scripts that create and use a per-user data folder; it does not request credentials, contact external endpoints, or install remote code, though it appears to be a lightweight/stub implementation rather than a full template repository.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim a personal template collection and reference ChristianLempa/boilerplates, but the included scripts are simple CLI stubs that manage a local data directory and logs—they do not ship or render template files. This is a functional mismatch (feature stub), but not a security incoherence.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running the provided commands. The scripts only read an optional BOILERPLATES_DIR env var, create a data directory, and read/write local files (data.log, history.log, config.json). There are no instructions to read unrelated system files or transmit data externally.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or remote downloads; this is instruction-only with bundled shell scripts. Nothing is fetched from external URLs or installed system-wide by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires no credentials or environment variables. It optionally uses BOILERPLATES_DIR to change the data directory—this is reasonable and documented. No unexpected SECRET/TOKEN env vars are requested or accessed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The scripts create and write files under a per-user data directory (default: ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/boilerplates). This is normal for CLI tools, but note that user-provided input (e.g., 'add' or 'run' arguments) is appended to logs/data files and will persist on disk.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is low-risk: it does not request credentials or perform network calls. Before running, review the bundled scripts (already included) and be aware they will create and write files under ~/.local/share/boilerplates by default (changeable with BOILERPLATES_DIR). Functionally, the package appears to be a stub/utility rather than a full template library—expect limited functionality. If you plan to run it, do so in a normal user account or sandbox and avoid passing sensitive data to commands because arguments are logged to history.log and data.log.
